requiredConcepts: The study compares age at first MMR vaccination in children with autism and school-matched controls.
Vaccination before 18 months or before 24 months was not associated with autism case status in the overall sample or evaluated subgroups.
Vaccination before 36 months was more common among cases in the total sample, but the authors attribute this likely to immunization requirements for early-intervention enrollment.
The birth-certificate subsample estimate for vaccination before 36 months was lower and its confidence interval included no association.
requiredPillars: Population-based case-control design and school matching
Results at the prespecified 18-, 24-, and 36-month cutoffs
Regression and other clinical subgroup results
Study limitations and the authors' explanation of the 36-month finding
